editorial:
When oil is found on Osage Nation land in 1920s Oklahoma, the Osage people become some of the richest in the world. But that wealth draws greedy outsiders who will do anything to get their hands on it. You follow Ernest Burkhart, a World War I veteran who marries Mollie Kyle, an Osage woman, while his uncle William Hale runs a secret plan to murder Osage people and steal their oil rights. The movie pulls you into a dark, slow-burning story about greed, love, and betrayal. It feels heavy and real.

Leonardo DiCaprio and Lily Gladstone give powerful performances that carry the whole film, and Robert De Niro is chilling as the manipulative uncle. The pacing is slow and deliberate, which works for the story but may test your patience if you want fast action. The cinematography is gorgeous, and the music adds to the tension. The downside is the long runtime, which can feel exhausting. If you enjoy true crime stories and historical dramas, this is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ernest finally confesses to his role in the murders after being pressured by the FBI. Mollie, who has been slowly poisoned by Ernest, survives and testifies against him. William Hale is arrested and convicted. The movie ends with a radio show reenacting the case, showing how the Osage murders were turned into entertainment. It is a sad reminder that real lives were lost and the story was never fully told.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true crime stories and historical dramas.
